It is referenced by neither .husky/pre-commit nor pre-push, so the never-delete-substance rule has not been enforced by anything; re-wiring the hook is the owner call. issues.note: RESOLVED AS A NAMED EXCEPTION — the second of the two options this item offered — and the board simply had not been updated to say so. `.tabsw` is registered in ALLOW_UNEQUAL in scripts/check-render.js carrying its argument: these are TABS IN A TABLIST, not a row of calls to action. THE SHARED .btn-row RECIPE WAS THE WRONG TOOL HERE and that is worth stating rather than leaving implied: btn-row exists because two CTAs of different label length are one decision and must not drift, which is a different claim from the one a tablist makes. Reviewed rather than inherited, per the standing rule that a prior decision is evidence and not authority: equal-width segments are a legitimate convention, so this is a live design choice rather than a defect, and it is flagged to the owner as such instead of being changed silently. See x

matches it while plainly being inline text. The owner’s rule — centre up to 3, left beyond — therefore had to be applied to FAMILIES by judgement, and the short members of those families go left with the long ones. issues.title: [hidden] display:none has now been restated in FIVE separate places
issues.note:
IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED 2026-08-04, and the sweep found MORE than the ticket knew about — SEVEN restatements, not five. The ticket named CommandPalette, TabSwitcher, faq.astro, pricing.astro and glossary/index.astro; /tools/ppn-002-calculator carried two more (.calc__err and .result). All seven deleted. tokens.css now carries ONE unlayered rule: [hidden]:not([hidden=until-found]) { display: none !important }. UNLAYERED IS LOAD-BEARING — a layered rule loses to any unlayered author rule regardless of !important, and this tree still has unlayered component styles. The until-found escape hatch is preserved so find-in-page can still reveal a collapsed region. PROVED IN A BROWSER rather than reasoned about: on /glossary a .gx-term computes display flex, and setting hidden on it takes it to display none with ZERO painted rects — which is the exact defect O-19 was, where the script set hidden on 18 cards and the browser drew all 24. Also proved on /tools/ppn-002-calculator, a route that now has no local rule at all.

PRIOR RECORD — OWNER DECISION 2026-08-04. VERDICT: put the central rule in tokens.css WITH !important, and delete all five local restatements. This is the one case where !important is correct — it restores a user-agent semantic that authors keep accidentally overriding, and it is the standard published fix. Sitewide reach across 43 routes is the POINT, not the objection. ACTION: one rule in tokens.css; remove the restatements in TabSwitcher.astro, CommandPalette.astro, faq.astro, forms.css (twice) and Glossary.astro.

PRIOR RECORD — TabSwitcher.astro, CommandPalette.astro, faq.astro, forms.css twice, and now glossary. issues.title: Geometry measured below the fold reads the arrival animation, not the layout
issues.note: THE FALSIFICATION PASS PRODUCED FIVE FALSE FAILURES AND ALL OF THEM WERE THIS. The arrival animations on this site run on a SCROLL timeline — animation-timeline: view(). They are not one-shot: an element below the fold sits at its FROM keyframe, RETURNS there when you scroll away again, and reports playState "running" with currentTime NaN and duration auto the entire time. So every getBoundingClientRect() taken on an element outside its view range reads the PRE-ARRIVAL TRANSFORM RATHER THAN THE LAYOUT. On /about that fabricated a 30.8px offset between a heading and its artefact card — which is EXACTLY the defect O-46 had been reported as, so the harness appeared to have found a regression it had in fact invented. On /faq it fabricated a 27.2px seam between two groups by differencing two neighbouring sections at different points in their travel (translateY 0.33 against 27.5). A first attempt to explain that seam blamed a stray one-character text node in <main>; removing all seven such nodes in the live page moved the gap by 0.0px, which is why the cause was tested rather than asserted. THE RULE, and it applies to every future audit of this site: measure geometry EITHER under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, where tokens.css collapses the durations and the transforms resolve to none, OR via offsetTop/offsetHeight, which are layout and ignore transforms by definition. Scroll into view only when the question is genuinely about paint. THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THE RECORD IS LARGER THAN THIS ITEM: any earlier measurement on this site taken with getBoundingClientRect against an element below the first screen is suspect in the same way, including figures in AUDIT-2026-08-03.md. Re-measure before treating any of them as evidence. This is a sibling of the recorded hidden-tab trap, where a background tab froze transitions and produced false blank-section reports: both are cases of the measurement apparatus changing what it measures.

All three readings are correct and all three disagree. This produced a contradiction between two of my own runs in the same session, which was chased as a caching fault and a post-load race before the token was read — the source settled in one grep what four browser runs could not. IT ALSO EXPLAINS A-18 ENTIRELY: its "63px" group is 7vh at 900px, i.e. the separate and deliberate --sec-pad-y-sm, used by Compare, Glossary, Sector and pricing. THE RULE: quote the TOKEN, not the pixel, and state viewport height whenever a pixel is unavoidable. Sibling of A-77 (geometry below the fold reads the arrival animation) — both are cases where the measurement setup, not the site, decided the number.

(a) astro/src/content/legal/terms.md:27 still says "Free plan usage is subject to monthly quota limits" - this is the original defect and it is CONFIRMED STILL PRESENT. Terms contracts for a free plan the business does not offer. (b) astro/src/data/pricing.ts:196 says "CrowMark is a paid product and there is no free plan", which agrees with the owner. (c) ProofGate.astro:100 says "Access is by request. There is no free plan and no self-serve trial." THE APPARENT CONFLICT WITH THE OWNER RESOLVES, AND IT MATTERS THAT IT DOES: a free trial granted ON REQUEST is not a SELF-SERVE trial, so "no self-serve trial" and "there is a free trial" are both true at once and neither line has to be withdrawn. (d) A-54 previously REMOVED the claim "All paid plans include a 14-day free trial" from the FAQ because it was not backed. WHAT IS SETTLED: Terms must stop contracting for a free plan. WHAT IS NOT, AND MUST NOT BE INVENTED: the trial's actual terms - length, whether a card is taken, whether it is per plan. A-54 was raised precisely because a duration was published that nothing backed, so no number goes back on the site until the owner states it. || DEEP DIVE COMPLETE 2026-08-05, and TWO VERIFIED FINDINGS CHANGE THE FRAMING. FIRST, A-54's stated premise was WRONG: the trial is not "a commitment nobody intended to honour" - the platform builds, grants and enforces it in three places and tells live customers "start a 14-day trial". What was unbacked was the WEBSITE'S version of it: card-free, self-serve, Pro-tier and uncapped. SECOND, the live site still publishes that unbacked version; see A-126, which is a P1 in its own right. RECOMMENDATION, every figure read from a constant already in production rather than chosen: 14 days, CrowMark STARTER scope, 3 users, 200 AI credits a month, NO CARD, granted on request. Documents bounded by the existing published rule of 3 credits per 10 pages rather than by a document count, because NO DOCUMENT COUNTER EXISTS (verified). Withheld from trial: the Pro surfaces, meaning delivery tracking, monthly social value reports and the s.52/s.71 checks. At expiry access stops and data is retained. NO CARD, AND THE REASONING IS NOT CONVERSION-LED: a card's only real jobs are qualifying the lead and deterring serial abuse, and invite-only signup plus a one-trial-per-work-email-domain ledger already do both server-side and fail closed, so a card buys a filter the product already has at the price of an unexpected charge landing on a public-sector buyer. THE HONEST GAP, WHICH BOUNDS WHAT MAY BE PUBLISHED: the day limit, expiry revocation, seat cap, one-per-domain rule and rate limits are all BUILT AND WORKING (verified). The generation cap is BUILT BUT ADVISORY - credit_accounting.py defaults CREDIT_ENFORCEMENT_MODE to "observe", and the flip to "enforce" is owner-gated in the R2.6.1 ledger pending real numbers. The deployed Railway value could NOT be read (the call was blocked), so it is UNCONFIRMED. PUBLISHING A CREDIT NUMBER BEFORE CONFIRMING THAT FLIP WOULD RECREATE THE A-54 DEFECT EXACTLY, which is the single most important sentence in this note. TWO VERIFIED LOOPHOLES, both matching the owner's own worry about a reader who "identifies a loop hole and keeps exploiting": the credit ledger buckets by CALENDAR MONTH, so a trial straddling month-end receives two full allowances; and there is no trial-specific allowance, so a checkout trial at Pro carries 750 credits. HIGHEST-VALUE SINGLE CONTROL: flipping CREDIT_ENFORCEMENT_MODE to enforce. Every other control limits how many trials exist; only this one limits what a single trial can consume, which is precisely the risk named. ON THE SITE COPY: ProofGate.astro:100 does NOT need to change - "no free plan" and "no self-serve trial" both remain true, because a trial granted on request is not self-serve. Only terms.md:27 is actually wrong on the facts, plus a second easy-to-miss line at terms.md:38 ("all account types, free and paid") that was not in the original evidence. issues.title: Three routes scroll horizontally at 320px (WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow)
issues.note:
VERIFIED ON THE REBUILT SITE 2026-08-04: ZERO horizontal overflow across all 44 routes at 320 and 390. Both fixes hold and neither changed anything at 390, 834 or 1440.

PRIOR RECORD — ROOT CAUSE PROVED AND BOTH FIXES APPLIED 2026-08-04. Two independent causes, not one. (1) /sources/: .src is repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr)). A track floor cannot shrink below itself, so at a 320px viewport the grid asked for a 320px track inside a 280px container — computed track literally read 320px in a 280px box — and pushed the document 20px sideways. Fixed with the canonical guard minmax(min(320px, 100%), 1fr), which is a no-op wherever there is room. Proved: track 320px -> 280px, overflow 20 -> 0. (2) /crowmark/ and /crowmark-buyers/: p.pcar__caption paints 338.3px wide at a 320px viewport, left -9.2, right 329.2. Fixed with overflow-x: clip on .pcar. CLIP RATHER THAN HIDDEN is load-bearing — clip creates no scroll container, so it cannot trap page scroll, cannot break position:sticky on an ancestor, and does not disturb the carousel’s own slide mechanism. Proved: 9 -> 0 on both routes. REGRESSION GUARD: both fixes measured at 390, 834 and 1440 and every route stayed at 0 — nothing changes at any width a reader is already served. I MUST CORRECT MY OWN EARLIER RECORD. This item previously said two hypotheses were “DISPROVED BY EXPERIMENT”. THEY WERE NOT DISPROVED — THEY WERE NEVER TESTED. Every one of those trials injected a rule like `.src { … }` at specificity (0,1,0) against Astro’s scoped `.src.astro-xxxx` at (0,2,0), so the test rule simply LOST and a correct hypothesis read as refuted. Re-running the identical rule with !important took the track to 280px and the overflow to 0 immediately. THE GENERAL LESSON, and it is the third measurement trap of the session after A-77 and A-79: ON THIS SITE, CSS INJECTED BY addStyleTag LOSES TO EVERY ASTRO-SCOPED RULE. A negative result from an injected probe means “my rule lost” until proved otherwise, never “the hypothesis is wrong”. Probe with !important, or read the computed value back to confirm the declaration actually applied — which is what finally settled this. STILL OPEN AS A SYSTEMIC QUESTION, recorded rather than swept: five more hardcoded auto-fit/auto-fill floors exist — glossary/index.astro 290px and 260px, sectors/index.astro 280px, styles/prose.css 260px, NavDropdown.astro 320px. Only floors above 280px can overflow at 320 once the 20px gutters are counted, and none of those routes overflowed in the sweep, so none is a confirmed defect. They are the same shape of latent bug and the min() guard is a no-op on all of them. Not touched this pass: NavDropdown.astro was held by another agent.

PRIOR RECORD — FOUND 2026-08-04 by a responsiveness sweep of every route at 320 and 390. 88 route-viewport pairs measured under reduced motion. AT 390 NOTHING OVERFLOWS — zero routes, which is why the existing audits never saw this: they use 1440/834/390 and the floor is 390. WCAG 1.4.10 specifies 320 CSS px, so this is a real AA criterion the build chain does not cover. THE DOCUMENT ITSELF SCROLLS, which is the test that matters — documentElement.scrollWidth exceeds clientWidth, so content inside a legitimate overflow-x:auto wrapper is excluded by construction. /crowmark/ +9px, /crowmark-buyers/ +9px, /sources/ +20px. MEASURED CULPRITS, after excluding every element clipped by an ancestor: on both crowmark routes exactly ONE unclipped element, p.pcar__caption — width 338.3px in a 320px viewport, left -9.2, right 329.2. On /sources/ SEVEN, all article.src__card — each exactly 320px wide starting at x=20, so right=340 against a 320px viewport. TWO HYPOTHESES RAISED AND BOTH DISPROVED BY EXPERIMENT, recorded so nobody repeats them. (1) The decorative .amb ambient field: injecting display:none on it left the overflow at 9px unchanged, so it is NOT the cause despite bleeding past the gutter by design. (2) min-width:0 on .src__card and max-width:100% on .pcar__caption: both left the overflow unchanged at 320 while remaining harmless at 390 and 1440. .pcar__caption ALREADY carries min-width:0 in components/ui/Carousel.astro with a comment about the flex min-width:auto trap, so that avenue was already taken. MY FIRST DETECTOR WAS ALSO WRONG and that is worth recording: it treated only overflow-x auto|scroll as clipping and ignored hidden and clip, so it blamed decorative <b> particles that .amb was clipping all along. The corrected detector checks all four values. NOT FIXED, deliberately: the remaining candidate is a hardcoded 320px floor in a grid track — article.src__card measuring EXACTLY 320 at a 320 viewport is the signature of minmax(320px, 1fr) with no min() guard — but that has not been proved yet, and this item has already produced two confident wrong answers. It gets proved before it gets changed. crowmark.astro was also held by another agent during this pass.

issues.title: A page namespace turned the icon-slot rule into a rule about every sized box on the biggest route
issues.note: FOUND BY A BUILD FAILURE 2026-08-04, immediately after ADR 0010 moved crowmark.astro’s scoped <style> into styles/crowmark.css and anchored all 192 selectors under .pg-crowmark. check-design-system.js matched icon selectors with /(logo|icon|mark|glyph|avatar) /i — TRAILING word boundary only, no leading one. So “mark” matched inside “.pg-crowmark”, and the moment every rule on the largest route in the site gained that prefix, a rule about ICON MODIFIERS became a rule about EVERY SIZED BOX ON /crowmark. It failed the build on .mech__chip:last-child::after, a 1px by 22px connector drawn at top:-22px to tie a commitment to the artefact proving it. TWO FIXES, BOTH COMPUTED RATHER THAN LISTED, because an allow-list entry here would have been a gate agreeing not to look at the largest route it covers. (1) The token must now START a word in a class name — at the start, or after a dot, hyphen, underscore or space — so .card__icon--sm and .logo--lg still match and crowmark does not. (2) AN OUT-OF-FLOW BOX CANNOT RESIZE A SLOT: a rule declaring position absolute or fixed is skipped, because by definition it is out of its parent’s flow and its width and height cannot shrink the slot the rule protects. That excuses the next connector, badge or rule-line on its merits without anybody listing it. PROVED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, against the real tree since this gate has no source override: PASS — clean, exit 0. FAIL — a temporary probe file carrying an in-flow .card__icon--sm { width:14px; height:14px } produced exit 1 naming both declarations, WHILE the absolutely-positioned probe alongside it was correctly excused. So the rule still catches the defect it exists for and no longer catches the thing it never meant. Probe file deleted. WORTH GENERALISING: a page-level namespace is a cheap and correct architectural move, and it silently changed what a REGEX-BASED gate matches. Any gate that reads selectors as text is exposed to this the day a namespace arrives.

issues.title: Mobile audit: a 10px footer chip and 18 standalone links under the 24px target floor
issues.note:
CORRECTED 2026-08-04 — THE FIRST VALUE WAS ON THE BOUNDARY AND FLAKED, exactly as A-74 warned. padding-block shipped at 3px, which took the 20px links to 26px and passed. But a shorter 18px link on the /compare routes became EXACTLY 24.00, and check-render reported it BELOW the floor on one run and clean on the next with no code change between them. The variable is font metrics: before the web font settles the fallback face gives a slightly shorter line box, so the same element measures 23.9 then 24.1. Now 4px, which puts the two populations on 26px and 28px. Neither can round to the wrong side of 24, so the rule is decided by geometry rather than by timing. Costs 2px more hit area on inline links and changes no layout at all, because padding on an inline box does not grow the line box. THE LESSON IS WORTH MORE THAN THE PIXEL: A PASSING GATE RUN IS NOT EVIDENCE THAT A VALUE ON THE BOUNDARY IS SAFE. The 3px version passed the run it was written in, and would have shipped. It was caught only because a later build failed on it and the failure did not reproduce when re-run — a disappearing failure is a flake, and a flake on a threshold means the value is sitting on it. PRIOR RECORD — VERIFIED ON THE RENDERED PAGE 2026-08-04 at 390: .ca-footer-free-chip computes 12px, clear of the legibility floor it sat two pixels under, and ZERO standalone targets remain under 24px. The build chain now prints “every target clears 24px” as part of its own summary. PRIOR RECORD — FULL MOBILE PASS 2026-08-04 — 44 routes at 320/360/390/414 with touch emulation and reduced motion, 2,193 interactive controls measured at 390. CLEAN: zero routes missing a viewport meta, zero unclipped media wider than the viewport, zero inline fixed widths over 320px, mobile nav trigger 44x44 at all four widths, and zero horizontal overflow anywhere (A-81 having fixed the three that existed). TWO DEFECTS FOUND AND BOTH FIXED. (1) .ca-footer-free-chip rendered at a HARDCODED 10px on all 44 routes, below the floor this site states in its own labels.css: "12px is the legibility floor... a label smaller than the smallest size is not a smaller label, it is an unreadable one." It was uppercase with positive tracking, which spends legibility rather than buying it, and it was the exact defect check-design-system.js rule 4 exists for — a hardcoded font-size in a component — surviving because the value never joined the type scale. Now var(--t-micro). (2) 18 standalone links under 24px, fixed centrally in tokens.css with padding-block: 3px on a link that is the child of a flow container. WHY PADDING RATHER THAN A HEIGHT, because it is the whole design: these are INLINE boxes, so min-block-size does nothing to them, and inline-flex would tear a mid-sentence link out of its line. CSS cannot tell the two apart — :only-child counts ELEMENTS, so "

See this

" matches it while plainly being inline text. Padding enlarges the hit area 2.5.8 measures without enlarging the line box. 3px and not 2px because 20+2+2 lands on exactly 24.00 and A-74 records a box at exactly 24.00 flickering either side of the limit on sub-pixel rounding. Measured: /faq 4 -> 0, /terms 11 -> 0, first paragraph unmoved at y=187 on every route.

issues.title: Homepage integration chips fail WCAG 1.4.3 — contrast quoted against the wrong surface
issues.note:
FIXED AND PIXEL-VERIFIED 2026-08-04. All six chips now pass at both viewports — worst case 4.96:1 at 1440 and 5.03:1 at 390, against 4.5:1 required, up from 3.31:1 to 3.50:1. MEASURED THE SAME WAY THE DEFECT WAS FOUND, deliberately: screenshot, second screenshot with all text forced transparent, then sample true background pixels inside each text rect. A DOM ancestor walk cannot see the gradient these chips paint and reported 160 then 29 false positives on this site, so a DOM-based confirmation would have proved nothing.

PRIOR RECORD — THE ONLY CONFIRMED CONFORMANCE FAILURE in a forensic accessibility audit of all 44 routes. Six span.in__scope elements on the homepage measured 3.31:1 to 3.50:1 against the 4.5:1 required for 12-13px normal-weight text, failing at BOTH 1440 and 390 — twelve failing measurements. The best sample anywhere inside those text boxes was 4.32:1, so no part of the gradient passed. THE CAUSE IS A COMMENT THAT MEASURED THE WRONG PAIR, and that is worth more than the fix. The rule carried the note "--c-text-muted measures 9.88:1 on --c-bg". That figure is TRUE. It is also irrelevant: these chips do not sit on --c-bg, each paints its own teal gradient, sampled from rendered pixels at #3a5e69 to #3e5c69. A contrast ratio is a claim about a PAIR, and quoting it against the page background when the component paints its own is exactly how a real failure ships with a passing number written beside it. FIXED: rest moves to --c-text-sub, about 5.06:1 on that ground, and the hover lift moves up to --c-text so the chip still brightens rather than resolving to its own rest value. MEASUREMENT NOTE THAT SHOULD GOVERN ANY FUTURE CONTRAST GATE: this was found by PIXEL sampling — full-page screenshot, a second with all text forced transparent, then sampling true background pixels inside each text rect. Two DOM ancestor-walk methods produced 160 and then 29 FALSE POSITIVES on this site, because .btn--primary paints a gradient no ancestor walk can see. A DOM-only contrast gate here would have reported 160 defects of which 148 were artefacts of its own method.

issues.title: Reported: honeypot fields exposed to screen readers — DID NOT REPRODUCE
issues.note: REPORTED BY THE ACCESSIBILITY AUDIT AND REFUTED ON VERIFICATION. The finding was that #cp-website, #contact-nl-website and #pt-website are labelled "Website", are not display:none or visibility:hidden, and lack aria-hidden — so a virtual-cursor user could find and fill them and have their submission silently rejected. That would be a real harm, which is why it was checked rather than actioned. IT IS NOT TRUE. All three honeypots are wrapped in <div class="form__pot" aria-hidden="true"> and that attribute survives into the built HTML on /contact and /partners — read directly out of dist. aria-hidden applies to the whole subtree, so the input is out of the accessibility tree by inheritance and no virtual cursor reaches it. The audit appears to have tested the <input> for the attribute rather than its wrapper. The construction is also correct in the detail that usually gets this wrong: aria-hidden on a container with a FOCUSABLE descendant is an ARIA violation, and tabindex="-1" here means there is no focusable descendant. Verified separately by the same audit: not reached in 60 Tab presses. RECORDED RATHER THAN DISCARDED because a refuted finding is evidence too — the next audit that walks this markup will raise it again unless the answer is written down.

Adding the metric-matched ‘Jakarta Fallback’ to the font stack left CLS slightly WORSE (/compare/crowmark-vs-autogenai/ 0.1277 -> 0.1388), and the reason is precise: that fallback overrides ascent, descent and line-gap, which are VERTICAL metrics and fix line-box height. The shift is driven by `ch`, which is the HORIZONTAL ADVANCE of the “0” glyph, and none of those overrides touches it. Arial’s advance is about 0.556em against Plus Jakarta Sans at 0.708em, and size-adjust 99.12% cannot close a 27% gap. MEASURED DIRECTLY: ch goes 45.88px to 58.91px on swap, taking .section__title’s max-width from 733.765px to 942.49px, and the h1 re-wraps from 209px tall to 111px — everything below it moves. REAL FIX: 22ch -> 15.576em and 16ch -> 11.328em in styles/headings.css. The ratio is 0.70801 and is IDENTICAL for h1 and h2, both weight 700, so the rendered width does not change — it is the same measure expressed in a unit that cannot move, because em is font SIZE and font-size does not change when the face swaps. Needs a rebuild and a re-measure before this goes to FIXED.

PRIOR RECORD — THE SINGLE LARGEST CORE WEB VITALS DEFECT ON THE SITE, and it costs zero bytes so not one of the 29 gates can see it. MEASURED WITH A CONTROL, which is what makes it certain rather than plausible: with webfonts BLOCKED, sitewide CLS falls from 1.587 to 0.0018 at 1440 and from 0.871 to 0.0000 at 390. Nothing else on the site contributes measurable shift — images contribute zero, proven by the same control. Four routes sat over Google’s 0.1 threshold. Re-measured independently before fixing: /compare/crowmark-vs-autogenai/ 0.1277 and /compare/crowmark-vs-swiftbid/ 0.1081 at 1440. THE MECHANISM IS THE `ch` UNIT. .section__title caps at 22ch and 16ch, and ch is FONT-RELATIVE, so the resolved max-width changes the instant the real face arrives. On /compare/crowmark-vs-autogenai/ the h1 went from 766px wide and 209px tall to 942px wide and 111px tall — it re-wrapped, and everything below it moved. THE FIX WAS ALREADY IN THE STYLESHEET. styles/fonts.css declares a metric-matched fallback, ‘Jakarta Fallback’, engineered with size-adjust 99.12%, ascent-override 97.25%, descent-override 26.84% and line-gap-override 0% — built for precisely this defect. It appeared EXACTLY ONCE in the entire dist: its own @font-face. It was named in no font-family stack, so --font-display fell straight through to system-ui and the fallback never loaded. Added to the stack, before system-ui, because a fallback listed after the generic families is never reached. THE OTHER HALF, AND IT IS WORSE THAN THE FIRST: under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, CLS gets HIGHER, deterministically — routes over 0.1 go from 3 to 2 at 1440 but from 1 to 3 at 390, and /blog/social-value-portal-vs-crowmark/ triples from 0.0334 to 0.1141. With the arrival animation running, elements are still translated or partly transparent when the font swaps, so the shift is DISCOUNTED from the metric. The animation was never fixing the shift; it was hiding it from the instrument, and hiding it specifically from the readers who asked for less motion. Inter, the body face, has no metric-matched fallback at all. That is the remaining half of this defect and is not fixed here.

issues.note: ROOT CAUSE NOW ATTRIBUTED, 2026-08-04. It is no longer unattributed. THE FIX IS ITS OWN MEASURED JOB: deriving the four ascent/descent/line-gap/size-adjust overrides for Inter must be measured, because guessing them makes it worse in a way that LOOKS like a fix, which is exactly how the first A-92 attempt failed. Do not attempt without measuring. || DERIVATION ATTEMPTED 2026-08-04 AND THE METHOD WAS PROVED INVALID BY ITS OWN CONTROL. Real metrics read from the shipped woff2 files with fontkitten: Inter upm 2048, ascent 1984, descent -494, lineGap 0, xAvgCharWidth 1250. Arial upm 2048, ascent 1854, descent -434, lineGap 67, xAvgCharWidth 904. The standard formula size-adjust = avgWidth(web)/avgWidth(fallback) gives 138.27% for Inter on Arial. THAT NUMBER IS WRONG AND THE CONTROL IS HOW WE KNOW: re-deriving the ALREADY SHIPPED Jakarta Fallback by the same method should reproduce 99.12/97.25/26.84/0 and instead produced 130.27/79.68/17.04/0, out by 31.15pp on size-adjust. ROOT CAUSE OF THE BAD METHOD: OS/2 xAvgCharWidth IS NOT COMPARABLE ACROSS FONTS. Arial reports 904/2048 under the old weighted-lowercase-Latin definition; Inter reports 1250/2048 under the modern average-of-all-non-zero-width-glyphs definition. Comparing them claims Inter is 38 percent wider than Arial, which is false. THE CORRECT METHOD is to compute the average advance width over a FIXED character set read from hmtx/cmap on both faces, so the same definition applies to both, or to measure the two faces rendered. Do that before shipping any number. The vertical figures are sound in isolation (Inter ascent 1984/2048 = 96.88%, descent 494/2048 = 24.12%, lineGap 0) but each must be divided by the correct size-adjust, so they cannot be shipped until size-adjust is right. || ATTRIBUTED 2026-08-05, AND IT IS THREE FONTS RATHER THAN ONE. Control first: with all webfonts blocked, CLS is 0.0000 on all 11 routes at both viewports, so it remains 100 per cent font swap and no image, script or scroll cause exists. THREE FINDINGS BEYOND THE ASK, ALL VERIFIED. FIRST, THE TWO 1440 EXCEPTIONS ARE MISATTRIBUTED IN THE GATE ITSELF: check-cwv.js records both compare routes as an Inter swap re-wrapping the standfirst, but blocking Inter changes nothing, 0.1201 to 0.1197, while blocking Plus Jakarta Sans gives 0.0008 - and the standfirst does not re-wrap at all, its height is 68.63 in both states and it MOVES because the h1 grows 105.64 to 201.31. Both halves of the recorded reason are wrong, so two exceptions are being held open for a fix that would not move them. SECOND, A-100 is now measured rather than suspected; see A-131. THIRD, A GATE DEFECT: the "(node gone)" rows, including the top-ranked one in the report, are an artefact, because the gate ranks shift sources by absolute change in top edge and an element pushed past the viewport bottom gets a fully zeroed rect, so its delta always wins; a MutationObserver recorded ZERO DOM removals. The fix is to skip an empty rect when picking the worst source. issues.title: A stray */ inside a doc comment in HeroStack.astro silently blocked every build
issues.note: HeroStack.astro line 16 carried the literal sequence .stratum*/.plane*/ inside a /** */ block. The */ closed the comment early, which produced 1,318 astro check errors and an esbuild parse failure, so NOTHING could build. It also produced three phantom check-facts em-dash failures that cleared the moment the comment closed properly, which is the dangerous part: the visible symptom pointed at content, not at syntax. Fixed with a one-line spacing change; the original is at scratchpad/HeroStack.astro.orig and was deliberately NOT restored because another agent had edited on top of the fix. WHY THIS STAYS OPEN AS A CLASS RATHER THAN A FIXED INSTANCE: this repo writes very long argued comments containing CSS selectors, and any selector ending in a star followed by a slash will do this again. A cheap gate that scans .astro and .ts comment blocks for an embedded */ would make it impossible. Worth pairing with the existing rule that check-render.js comments may contain no backticks, which is the same class of defect. || FIXED 2026-08-05 WITH A GATE, AND THE GATE IMMEDIATELY EARNED ITS PLACE. astro/scripts/check-comment-terminators.js scans .astro, .ts, .js, .mjs and .css across src/ and scripts/ (140 files) for a */ that closes a block comment earlier than its author meant, and for unterminated comments. IT WAS PROVED ABLE TO FAIL BEFORE BEING TRUSTED, which is the standing rule for a new gate here. ON ITS FIRST REAL RUN IT FOUND AN UNKNOWN LIVE DEFECT: src/pages/roadmap.astro:628 carried an orphan terminator, so a doc comment closed early and three lines of English prose had been sitting in the stylesheet as CSS. Nobody had reported it and no other gate saw it. Fixed; the gate now exits 0 on a clean tree and 1 on the defect. NOTE ON HOW IT WAS ALMOST MISSED: a naive count of /* against */ flagged three OTHER files as broken and missed nothing real - all three were false positives from ** and /**. Counting delimiters is not scanning comment state, and the difference is the whole gate. || GATE DELIVERED AND PROVEN, 2026-08-05, and the defect it found was WORSE THAN REPORTED. It is a tokenising scanner rather than a grep, because "is this terminator inside a comment" is precisely the question a grep cannot answer: it tracks strings, template literals with substitutions, regex literals and both comment forms, and splits .astro into frontmatter, each style block, each script block and markup. Three detections: EARLY (the terminator actually typed), ORPHAN (the downstream wreckage) and UNTERMINATED. PROVED ABLE TO FAIL against a fixture reproducing the exact .stratum*/.plane*/ case, with a negative control on the fixed form reporting zero. The first version had EIGHTEEN false positives across nine files, because a regex found a style tag written INSIDE a Footer.astro comment; rewritten to walk the markup, it now reports zero on the tree. THE REAL DEFECT IT FOUND: roadmap.astro line 625 closed a 25-line CSS comment early, and the built stylesheet literally contained "the column was the wrong width for the chip. */ grid-template-columns: subgrid;" - so the malformed declaration ran to the first semicolon and SWALLOWED grid-template-columns: subgrid. IT MUST RUN FIRST, before check-facts.js, because the original incident produced three PHANTOM check-facts em-dash failures - prose after an accidental terminator stops being a comment, so a prose gate reads it as content. || WIRED 2026-08-05: check-comment-terminators.js is now step 1 of 32 in astro/package.json, ahead of check-facts.js for the reason the agent gave - a stray terminator makes the prose after it stop being a comment, so a prose gate reads it as content and reports failures that are not real. issues.title: check-glossary-filter fails only inside the full chain and passes standalone on the identical dist
issues.note: Its ONECLEAR rule BYTE-COMPARES TWO SCREENSHOTS. It failed four consecutive in-build runs, then passed 4 of 4 and 1 of 1 standalone against the SAME dist. So the gate is order- or environment-sensitive rather than measuring a real defect, and a byte comparison of two renders is the likely reason - antialiasing and compositing need not be bit-identical between runs. NOTE THE MIS-ATTRIBUTION, because it is the more useful lesson: the agent first blamed the starfield, tested that hypothesis, found it wrong, and corrected its own note in Base.astro. A flaky gate is worse than no gate, because it trains everyone to ignore a red build. Either make the comparison tolerant (a perceptual or per-channel threshold) or make it deterministic. ALSO RECORDED HERE: a full chain run died at gate 22 with EXIT 127 on check-controls.js, which is a SPAWN failure not a source fault - the file is present and node --check passes. Gates 23 to 29 were then each run individually against that exact dist and all returned EXIT 0. So all 29 gates have been OBSERVED green on this tree, but NOT in one uninterrupted process, and that distinction is deliberately recorded rather than rounded up to "green". || RENUMBERED FROM A-110 ON 2026-08-05. Two terminals were writing status/issues.json at the same time and both allocated A-110 and the id after it. Nothing was lost and no content changed; this entry moved so the pair logged from the Chrome audit could keep the numbers already written into the HowItRuns.astro and HeroStack.astro comments, which are the harder references to chase. If you are the other terminal and were looking for A-110, it is here. || REAL CAUSE FOUND AND FIXED PROPERLY, 2026-08-05, with no retry and no sleep. THREE HYPOTHESES RULED OUT BY TEST rather than by argument: port collision (every copy calls listen(0) and the chain is sequential, so the A-99 extraction does NOT fix this as a side effect - there was nothing there to fix), caret blink (caret-color: transparent produced an identical hash), and leftover state from an earlier gate (it reproduces standalone in a fresh process). THE ACTUAL CAUSE: the ONECLEAR rule compared two PNGs with Buffer.compare, which is exact. Measured over the 956x50 clip, eight pairs differed in zero pixels but one earlier pair differed in 21 pixels by EXACTLY 1/255, scattered - encoder noise, not a second control. An injected real defect moves 109 pixels past 8/255 with a peak of 231. So the signal and the noise are three orders of magnitude apart and the gate was thresholding at zero. Fixed by decoding both screenshots and thresholding on both axes, NOISE_CHANNEL 8 and MIN_GLYPH_PX 12: eight times above the measured noise and nine times below the measured glyph. Proved BOTH ways - clean gives 28/28 and "moves 0 of 47800 pixels past 8/255 (peak 0)" at exit 0; defect injected gives exit 1 and names the second control. The measurement now prints on every run, so the margin stays visible rather than being rediscovered.

issues.title: Ambient motion inventory: reportedly 95 animated elements across 21 keyframe animations running at once
issues.note: NOT YET VERIFIED BY ME, logged with its provenance rather than as fact. The audit counted 95 animated elements and 21 keyframe animations running concurrently and attributes the over-animated impression to always-on ambient motion (hue shift, drifting orbs, perpetual beams, decorative pulses) rather than to entrance or interaction motion. THIS IS THE SAME SURFACE AS A-103, which measured 23 elements painting radial gradients where the concept paints one, so the two should be fixed together and counted once. The audit also confirms 12 prefers-reduced-motion queries already exist, so the accessibility fallback is present and the change is editorial. TARGET PROPOSED: three or fewer continuous animations on screen at once, entrance and interaction motion kept. MEASURE FIRST with document.getAnimations() before cutting, so the count is ours and not inherited. || MEASURED 2026-08-05, Playwright Chromium against astro/dist, and the audit is CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Peak concurrent animations 89 across 82 elements at 1440 (audit said 95: right order, overstated). Distinct keyframe names 26, not 21 - two extras are short one-shots on long delays that any single snapshot misses. prefers-reduced-motion blocks 32, not 12: a raw grep returns 52 but 20 of those are prose inside comments, and the split matters more than the total, 23 no-preference gates against 9 reduce overrides. THE RAW TOTAL IS THE WRONG NUMBER TO ARGUE FROM: 31 of the 89 are scroll-driven, 1 ScrollTimeline and 30 ViewTimeline, which sit in getAnimations() permanently but only move while the reader scrolls, and they are the single largest source of inflation. THE HONEST ARRIVAL NUMBER IS 5: a reader landing at scrollY 0 sees five perpetual animations in view, four hero drift orbs and the hero eyebrow shimmer, out of 19 running document-wide. THE REAL DEFECT IS A RATCHET, and it is not what the audit described: section ambient loops start on reveal and are NEVER STOPPED, so the perpetual count climbs from 19 to 49 as the page is read and scrolling back to the top does not bring it down. Per section at 1440: Hero 5, MarketShape 8, BothSides 9, ReasoningTrace 12, Integrations 8, FinalCta 6, Footer 1, and ProofGate, ProductScreens and HowItRuns have ZERO. So the three newest sections are already clean and the cut belongs in the five older ones. REDUCED MOTION IS A CLEAN PASS, NOT A NEAR MISS: document.getAnimations() returns literally 0 at both viewports at every sample point, because ambient motion is gated INSIDE @media (prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference) so animationName computes to none rather than being zeroed after the fact. NOT MEASURED, STATED SO NOBODY ASSUMES IT WAS: hover and focus motion entirely (nothing was hovered, so zero CSSTransition objects were captured and interaction motion needs its own pass), Chromium only, and the duty cycle of the opacity-0 sweeps.

No section is exempt and no section states its own ground. It is two lines of unlayered CSS in pages/index.astro, on nth-of-type(odd) and (even), because position is the one fact only index.astro knows - so reordering sections now moves the surfaces with them and nothing else needs editing. FinalCta sits outside the ladder by construction rather than by exemption: it renders a div, not a section, so the selector cannot reach it. THE MEASUREMENT THAT FORCED THIS: before any change, all EIGHT sections on the built homepage reported rgb(3,4,10). THERE WAS NO ALTERNATION LEFT AT ALL. The cause was this session's own A-103 fix - moving --c-floor onto <html> turned .sv-floor into a no-op painting the exact ground it was meant to step off. Nobody had reported it because a flat page does not look broken, it just looks flat. The concept was then measured for the correct phase: html rgb(3,4,10), .band unpainted, .band-inset rgb(5,7,14), which is precisely the pair now implemented. HANDED BACK, NOT DELETED: class="sv-floor" is now dead on the homepage inside ProofGate, HowItRuns, BothSides and Integrations. issues.title: Two terminals write status/issues.json and astro/ concurrently with no coordination
issues.note: OBSERVED, NOT INFERRED, 2026-08-05. Two Claude terminals were working this tree at once. Three concrete consequences inside about twenty minutes: (1) BOTH allocated A-109 and A-110 to different issues, because the id is chosen by reading the current maximum and adding one, which is a read-modify-write with no lock; (2) the other terminal DELETED astro/scripts/measure-fidelity.mjs as a scratch script, judging it "referenced by nothing" - true of the gate chain, false of board item A-108, which exists to hold it, and it was restored from commit f7181465; (3) RESUME-HERE-2026-08-05.md was rewritten to describe a state that included this terminal's commit and its two agents' uncommitted edits, so the two sessions are documenting each other. THE UNDERLYING HAZARD IS NOT THE IDS. It is that status/issues.json is a whole-file rewrite: a concurrent write does not merge, it replaces, so the loser's entries vanish silently and the count still looks plausible. This time nothing was lost only because the writes happened to interleave between reads. WHAT WOULD FIX IT: allocate ids from a monotonic counter held in the file rather than from max+1, or write one entry per file under status/issues/ so two writers cannot collide on the same bytes. Until then, re-read the board immediately before every write and diff the ids you expected against the ids present. || FIXED 2026-08-05 by status/add-issue.js, and A-149 records the implementation. The id half is closed: allocation now comes from a monotonic nextId counter in the file, seeded once from the existing maximum and never consulted against it again, so an id is never reused even after a deletion. The script also validates severity and status, reading the valid statuses from the board LEGEND rather than restating them, so the validator cannot drift from the thing it enforces. IT WAS TESTED BY USING IT: A-149 was allocated by the script, the counter advanced to 150, and the board reports zero duplicate ids across 219 items. THE WHOLE-FILE-REWRITE HALF IS DELIBERATELY NOT CLOSED and the script header says so plainly: two processes writing at the same instant can still lose one another entries, and fixing that properly means one file per issue under status/issues/, which is more change than one collision justified. A guard now STOPS rather than overwrites if the counter and the file disagree, because a silent overwrite here is the failure mode with the worst properties - the loser entries vanish and the count still looks plausible.

issues.title: Competitor trial terms researched across 60+ bid, AI and document products
issues.note: RECORDED AS EVIDENCE so the trial numbers are not re-argued from scratch, and so the fabricated benchmarks that circulate on this topic are not pulled back in. WHAT THE MARKET ACTUALLY DOES: the direct bid/tender competitors mostly publish NO trial and NO price at all - Loopio, Responsive/RFPIO, Qvidian, AutogenAI, Arphie, Ombud, Rohirrim, GovDash and Tussell are all demo-gated. Those that do publish one cluster at 14 days. A large group skips the trial entirely for a perpetual CAPPED FREE TIER: Stotles 3 bid/no-bid reports lifetime, Bidhive 3 bids a month, TenderWolf a credit burn-down with a published rate card, BidWriter 3 AI credits a month. THE CLEANEST PRECEDENT FOR WHAT THE OWNER ASKED FOR is PandaDoc: 14 days AND 50 documents, two hard walls, whichever hits first, with a tighter cap again for personal-email signups. Docsumo is the same shape at 14 days and 1,000 pages. FOUR CAP ARCHETYPES ARE IN USE: time x work-units, time x seats, a burn-down credit with no clock, and a perpetual capped tier. EXPIRY WORDING WORTH COPYING, and this is the part most likely to be got wrong: nobody in the surveyed set DELETES at expiry, 10 of 12 downgrade to a capped free state, and the strongest wording names what SURVIVES rather than what dies - Qwilr keeps client-facing pages live for 30 days after expiry with editing locked, Proposify lets clients still view and accept proposals sent during the trial. Both are directly transferable to a bid tool. TWO WARNINGS ON THE NUMBERS: card-required trials do convert far better on paper (ChartMogul, Jan 2026, n=200: 25-35% against 4-6%), but opt-out rates are inflated BY DEFINITION because they count people who forgot to cancel, so they measure billing events rather than adoption. And the widely-quoted "conversion by trial length" figures (7d=24%, 14d=19%, 30d=14%), the "Gartner 20%" and "90% decide in 5 days" are UNSOURCED and were excluded as citation laundering; a large RCT (n=680,588, Jun 2025) found the LONGER trial converted 20.92% better, which is the opposite of the folklore. ChartMogul's own 62% figure is a POPULARITY distribution of trial lengths, not a performance one - anyone citing it for "14 beats 30" is over-reading it.

issues.title: --grad-beam and --grad-fade carried var() knobs that never worked, and three renders were silently wrong
issues.note: FOUND BY AN AGENT WORKING IN BothSides.astro, CONFIRMED AT SOURCE, FIXED 2026-08-05. Both tokens were declared on :root as linear-gradients containing var(--knob, fallback). A custom property has its var()s substituted where it is DECLARED, so on :root the fallbacks bake in and the finished token inherits; setting the knob on a descendant changes nothing because there is no var() left to answer. THIS SITE HAD ALREADY PAID FOR THIS LESSON ONCE: tokens.css records the identical mechanism for --grad-ramp, where it put an opaque rectangle over every blog hero photograph. THE FIX IS A VISUAL NO-OP BY CONSTRUCTION, because the fallbacks are exactly what has been rendering: the knobs are inlined so each token is honestly one fixed recipe. What changes is that the trap is no longer silent. A beam or rail needing a different hue, width or angle must now write its gradient at the point of use, which check-design-system rule 7 explicitly permits (it forbids a literal COLOUR in a gradient, not a gradient), and which .bs__cap already does and explains. LEFT DELIBERATELY UNFIXED: the three renders above are not corrected by this change, only made explicable. issues.title: Jakarta Fallback declared no font-weight, so every heading using it was a synthesised bold from Arial Regular
issues.note: MEASURED 2026-08-05 WHILE ATTRIBUTING A-96, AND HALF-FIXED DELIBERATELY. Two defects in one at-rule. FIRST, AND NOW FIXED: the @font-face declared NO font-weight descriptor, and an @font-face without one matches ONLY weight 400. Every heading that reaches this fallback is 700 or 800, so the browser was taking Arial Regular and SYNTHESISING a bold from it. A synthesised bold is wider than a real one and its metrics are not the ones the overrides were derived against, which is exactly how a metric-matched fallback stops matching. It now declares font-weight 100 900, deliberately wider than 700 800, because a range narrower than the family reintroduces the same synthesis at the edges. THIS IS THE SAME MISTAKE AS THE JETBRAINS MONO ONE FIXED HOURS EARLIER IN THE SAME FILE, where a variable face with a 400 to 800 axis was declared at only 400 and 500. Two faces, one lesson: an omitted @font-face descriptor is not a default, it is a restriction. SECOND, AND DELIBERATELY NOT FIXED: size-adjust claims 99.12 per cent while the fallback measures 9.61 per cent NARROWER than the real face at heading weights, 2174.4px against 1983.8px on the same string. The number is wrong and the shift it exists to prevent is partly still there. It is left alone because A-100 records exactly how these numbers went wrong the first time - derived from xAvgCharWidth, which is not comparable across fonts because Arial reports the old weighted-lowercase definition and modern faces the all-glyphs one, with a control re-derivation missing by 31 percentage points - and the candidate replacement of about 108.64 per cent is arithmetic on a SINGLE string and explicitly not shippable. There is also an ordering constraint that makes fixing it now actively wrong: any re-derivation performed before the weight descriptor was corrected would have measured the SYNTHESIS rather than the face. Re-derive over a fixed character set across the real weight range, with a control, and only then change that line.

THE MOVE BROKE THE FLOOR ALTERNATION IMMEDIATELY, exactly as both files had predicted in their own comments: the buyer page put two floor sections side by side, and the supplier page carried a long note explaining that inserting the showcase had already shifted the parity of every section below it and that the resulting break had been deliberately placed at the end. Both notes described the cost of a HAND-PLACED ladder without preventing it, and this would have been the third time /crowmark paid it. So eight classes on the supplier page and five on the buyer page were REMOVED and replaced by the position-derived rule already added to the homepage under A-118: odd sections paint nothing, even sections paint --c-bg, and moving a section now moves its surface with it. RECORDED HONESTLY: on /crowmark this splits the four capability sections, so fit and citation are drawn before the screens and refusal and delivery after. The old argument for the old position, that all four drawings should be checkable against the interface immediately after them, is kept in the file beside the new one rather than deleted, because it was a real argument.

issues.title: Statutory figures numeral reduced from 108px to 80px
issues.note: OWNER 2026-08-05 on the built homepage: "in home page Statutory figures do you think it must that big, i dont think so hence reduce the size of figures, look so big?" --t-numeral was clamp(3.25rem, 7.4vw, 6.75rem), reaching 108px at 1440; it is now clamp(2.75rem, 5.6vw, 5rem), reaching 80px. THE CASE FOR 108px WAS ALREADY HALF-WITHDRAWN, which is why this needed no argument: tokens.css records that the 128px proposal rested on a MIS-MEASUREMENT, betterstack.com being cited as the precedent for an enormous numeral when its figure actually renders at 14px, and that external half was withdrawn on 2026-08-03. What survived was our own reasoning, that a stat inverts the usual hierarchy and a ratio of 1.24 to the heading above is not an inversion. That reasoning argues for a figure LARGER than its heading, not for the largest figure that fits. At 80px the ratio to the 46.4px section heading is 1.72, still an inversion; at 108px it was 2.33. The arithmetic constraint the old value was pinned to, "the largest value that fits a 208px column", is satisfied with room to spare. THE TABLET OVERRIDE CAME DOWN WITH IT, and would have been a defect if left: MarketShape carried its own clamp(3.5rem, 11vw, 7.5rem) at two columns, a 120px ceiling LARGER than the desktop token ever reached, so lowering only the token would have made the tablet width the loudest place on the site. issues.title: The trust band chips failed WCAG AA at 4.03:1, and A-84 recorded the wrong figure
issues.note: FOUND BY THE GRADIENT AUDIT 2026-08-05, FIXED THE SAME DAY, and it was failing two rules at once. The chip painted two backgrounds: a fill clipped to the padding box over --grad-edge on the border box, and the rule's own comment claimed "the ramp shows only in the 1px the border occupies". IT NEVER DID. The fill was color-mix(--c-ambient-start 5%, --c-card) over --c-card, and --c-card is rgba(255,255,255,0.05), so the whole fill computed to about 10 per cent alpha and --grad-edge, teal at 48 per cent and violet at 34 per cent, read straight through the face of every chip. Measured from DECODED PIXELS the face was #317174, a saturated teal, putting --c-text-sub on it at 4.03:1 against the 4.5:1 WCAG 1.4.3 requires. A-84 recorded 5.06:1 for this element; that figure was taken from the token rather than from the rendered pixels and is WRONG. THE SECOND RULE BROKEN was one semantic per hue: teal means verified and violet means refused, and a connector list was wearing both as decoration. FIXED by making the padding-box fill opaque, which simply makes the code do what its comment already said: linear-gradient(--c-raised, --c-panel 78%), two opaque steps of the same neutral, luminance only and no hue, which is exactly the treatment the approved gradient rule requires under text. Measured after: 13.33:1 for --c-text-sub, 18.53:1 for white and 9.10:1 for --c-text-muted, at BOTH ends of the ramp. The 5 per cent ambient tint went with it, deliberately: a chip carrying two lines of text is precisely where a hue does not belong.

issues.title: The Cloudflare check is not missing from the contact forms; it loads on first interaction
issues.note: OWNER REPORTED 2026-08-05: "why cloudflare check is missing from all the contact forms?" IT IS NOT MISSING, and this was established by driving the built page rather than by reading the code. Measured on /contact/: on page load the holder is present with data-sitekey null, zero children and ZERO requests to Cloudflare; after focusing the first field the sitekey is written, the widget renders one child and six Cloudflare requests are made. Turnstile.astro is wired into ContactForm, NewsletterForm and PartnerForm, both site keys are configured, and the CSP allows challenges.cloudflare.com in script-src and frame-src. THE LOAD IS DELIBERATELY DEFERRED TO focusin so no third-party request happens until a reader actually starts filling the form, which is a real privacy and performance benefit. Submission is still gated, because focusin fires on the submit button too, so there is no path to submitting without the check. WHAT IS GENUINELY TRUE IN THE REPORT is the perception: a reader looking at a contact form sees no security affordance at all, which on a form that collects an enquiry reads as unprotected. OFFERED TO THE OWNER, NOT DONE: keep the lazy load and add one line telling the reader the check appears when they start typing, which keeps the engineering benefit and answers the perception. Rendering it eagerly is the alternative and costs a third-party request on every page carrying a form.
