issues.title: The footer trust row ticked five security claims in the VERIFIED hue, including one whose own footnote says it is not certified
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 VIA AN EXTERNAL REVIEW, THOUGH NOT THE DEFECT THAT REVIEW THOUGHT IT HAD FOUND. The footer trust row lists AES-256 at rest, TLS 1.3, UK and EU residency, ISO 27001 controls and ICO registered, each preceded by a tick drawn with stroke="var(--c-verified)". TEAL MEANS VERIFIED ON THIS SITE AND NOTHING ELSE. Four lines below the row, its own footnote reads "We follow ISO 27001 controls. We are not certified yet." So the drawing asserted verified while the small print denied certification, about the same claim, four lines apart. THE WORDS WERE ALWAYS HONEST; THE TICK WAS DOING THE OVERCLAIMING, which is the exact shape the owner has ruled out twice - A-104 item 9, "an unbacked badge is WORSE than the six cards it replaces", and A-114, "must not add any false so ignore this". FIXED by taking the tick to --c-text-muted so it reads as a bullet rather than an assertion. The five claims and the footnote are unchanged; what is gone is a semantic hue certifying an uncertified claim. check-palette-roles green. NOTE HOW IT WAS FOUND, because it generalises: the reviewer read the page as PLAIN TEXT, which stripped the ticks entirely and left the five claims sitting together as a list - and then recommended formatting them as "a clean checklist or badge row", which is the opposite of what they needed. It reached a real defect from a wrong premise.

issues.title: The same /cookie-preferences link rendered twice in one footer
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 by an external review reading the footer as plain text, which is precisely how a duplicate fifteen links apart becomes obvious - laid out and spread across two regions, the eye does not catch it. data/footer.ts carried "Cookie preferences" in the Legal column AND in bottomLinks, so the identical href rendered twice on every route. REMOVED FROM THE LEGAL COLUMN, kept in the bottom bar, and the split is the reason rather than a coin toss: "Cookies" is the POLICY and belongs with Security, Privacy and Terms; "Cookie preferences" is a CONTROL that changes a setting and belongs beside Status, which is the conventional place a reader looks for it.

issues.title: External review reported the homepage as having no headings, no sections and no lists; it had read a text extract
issues.note: ASSESSED AND LARGELY REFUTED 2026-08-05, recorded so the same review is not actioned twice. An external reviewer described the homepage as "one long block" with "no h1, h2, h3 hierarchy", "no section grouping", "no ul or ol lists", "no headings for screen readers" and "no ARIA landmarks", and called this "the biggest conversion blocker". MEASURED ON THE BUILT PAGE: exactly ONE h1, TEN h2, FIFTEEN h3, NINE section elements and SIX lists. Every structural claim is false. THE CAUSE IS THE SAME ONE THAT HAS PRODUCED FALSE READINGS ON THIS SITE ALL SESSION: it read a proxy for the page rather than the page. A text extract has no CSS, so of course it reads as one undifferentiated block; that is a description of text extraction, not of the document. TWO OTHER ITEMS ARE THE SAME ARTEFACT. "The Sources section repeats permissions twice" is the trust band marquee's aria-hidden clone, invisible to both readers and screen readers. "Pause scrolling appears as literal text, an internal placeholder" is the WCAG 2.2.2 pause control, correctly labelled, whose icon does not exist in a text dump. TWO FINDINGS WERE REAL AND ARE FIXED SEPARATELY: A-140 and A-141. THE LESSON WORTH KEEPING is not that the review was useless - it found two genuine defects - but that a reviewer working from a text extract will systematically report structure as missing and will systematically miss anything visual, so its structural findings need measuring before any of them is believed.

issues.title: Four sector pages declared image dimensions that did not match the files, so each reserved the wrong box and shifted on load
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 while swapping the screens, and it is a CLS defect nobody was looking for. Every one of the four sector pages carried width and height attributes that disagreed with the actual file: construction and education declared 2360x1180 and education 2360x1180 at a ratio of 2.0, facilities 2464x1232 also 2.0, and highways 2464x904 at 2.726 - while every one of those images was really 1440x900, a ratio of 1.6. The attributes exist to reserve the correct box before the image arrives, so a wrong ratio means the reserved box is the wrong SHAPE and the page reflows the moment the image decodes. Highways was the worst, reserving a box nearly 1.7 times too wide for its height. The four compare pages were honest by contrast, declaring 1440x900 and 1024x768 correctly. All eight now carry dimensions MEASURED from the decoded file with sharp rather than copied from a name. NOTE THE INTERACTION WITH A-96: that item attributed the residual CLS entirely to the font swap after a control showed zero shift with webfonts blocked. That control was run on eleven routes and the four sector pages were not among them, so this is a second, independent CLS source on routes the control never covered.

issues.title: Four image captions described things that were not in the images they sat under
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 by opening every image rather than trusting its filename or its existing caption. FOUR CAPTIONS WERE FACTUALLY FALSE. highways.md described "an advisory s.52 KPI check ... marked Not applicable" which appears NOWHERE on the image it was attached to. crowmark-vs-mytender-io.md described "a PPN 002 mission mapping" whose "missions are the government's own ... and stay editable" - there are no missions on that screen at all. Both captions had been written against what the FILENAME suggested rather than against the picture, and both filenames were themselves wrong (see A-139). TWO MORE CUT AGAINST A STANDING RULE rather than against the pixels: construction claimed "the notices themselves are genuine published Find a Tender and Contracts Finder records", which cannot be verified and which OA-16 forbids because it asserts the drawing is live data; and facilities and cleantender both used "sample account's own data" and "sample data from that account", which is precisely the inline "sample data" label the owner's 2026-08-03 decision rules out. All four now use the canonical framing recorded in data/crowmark-screens.ts: the screens are drawn representations and the figures on them are part of the drawing. THE GENERAL LESSON IS THE ONE THIS SESSION KEEPS RELEARNING: alt text and captions written from a filename describe a file, not an image, and only opening the image catches it.

issues.title: The card hover defect was never brightness, it was AREA: 1232px containers were taking the full card hover
issues.note: THREE PREVIOUS ROUNDS TUNED THE WRONG PROPERTY, which is why the owner kept reporting it unfixed. O-34 restored the sheen, O-37 moved its core to white, O-66 halved its alpha - all about how BRIGHT the hover is. The defect was how BIG it is. MEASURED on figure.spine__panel, a 1232px block: backgroundColor went from the opaque rgb(12,16,32) to rgba(255,255,255,0.05), so the panel turned to glass; borderTopColor went from 12 per cent white to PURE WHITE on all four sides; transform lifted it 2px; and the ::after swept a 2460px band. The same on .hir, .ps__showcase and figure.spec. AND BECAUSE :hover MATCHES ANCESTORS it fired from anywhere inside, so pointing at one 219px step card lifted the step AND the 1232px panel beneath it: two lifts, two white edges, two bands, from one pointer. FIXED CENTRALLY rather than per component: .surface:has(.surface) - a container - and figure.surface - a drawing - reset border-color, box-shadow and transform, and generate no band. Written as TWO rules rather than one comma list on purpose, because an unsupported :has() invalidates its whole selector list and the figure half must survive that. THREE THINGS THIS CORRECTED ALONG THE WAY. A CODE COMMENT WAS LYING: .surface--panel:hover said "A PANEL STILL DOES NOT LIFT ... Delete this rule and panels start lifting again", and it only ever set box-shadow, so panels were lifting WITH the rule in place - and I had trusted that comment when editing the rule hours earlier. check-sheen IS SOUND and my doubt was wrong: MEAN_DELTA is a FLOOR, not a ceiling, so 3.223/2.270/2.753 against 1.0 are passes; the gate simply never looked at a container. And the only touch-latch on the site was found in the same sweep, 2 of 189 signatures, both in TabSwitcher, where a tap latched :hover so the last-tapped tab stayed lit while a different tab carried aria-selected. REGRESSION SWEEP: 191 hover signatures across five routes, zero now change any computed LAYOUT property, zero introduce a hue, zero latch; 83 signatures under reduced motion, zero elements move.

issues.title: Semantic hues were appearing on hover states in three places, hidden by token naming
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 across two independent audits. .sv-raised:hover opened a 42px glow at color-mix(--c-ambient-deep 26%), which resolves to #7C3AED - VIOLET, the refusal semantic - so nine drawn panels lit as refused because a mouse moved. .in__chip:hover carried BOTH: a 7 per cent teal tint in the fill, a 26px teal glow at 22 per cent, and a 38 per cent VIOLET cast shadow, on six connector chips. WHY IT SURVIVED SO LONG IS THE USEFUL PART, and it is a naming problem rather than a discipline one: the tokens are named for the AMBIENT FIELD they belong to, --c-ambient-start and --c-ambient-deep, so at the call site neither reads as "the verified colour" or "the refusal colour". Nobody writing color-mix(--c-ambient-deep 26%) sees themselves writing violet. ALL NOW RESOLVE FROM --c-interactive, which V6 puts at white, making every lit state a LUMINANCE change - exactly what the gradient rule approved the same day permits. Two alphas were re-derived by measurement rather than carried across, because white at a saturated hue's alpha reads far brighter: violet 26 per cent gave a 1.2706 mean channel delta and white 14 per cent gives 1.2582, within 1 per cent; the chip glow came down 22 to 12 on the same reasoning. The chip's cast shadow took --c-floor rather than white: a shadow is an absence of light, so a white one was wrong regardless of the hue rule. A FOURTH WAS FOUND ALREADY FIXED: motion.css recorded .prose a:hover turning the site's highest-volume link teal, and prose.css now reads --c-text. That stale note was corrected rather than deleted, because a "known defect" that is no longer true makes a reader either re-fix it or stop trusting the defects recorded beside it.

issues.title: The mobile nav fix hid nothing: two scoped rules tied on specificity and Button won, giving every route horizontal scroll at 390
issues.note: A REGRESSION INTRODUCED BY THE FIX FOR THE MISSING SEARCH ICON, 2026-08-05, and caught by two independent detectors within the hour. Nav.astro replaced a rule hiding the whole .ca-nav-actions container with one naming .ca-nav-login and .ca-nav-cta directly. Those two are classes handed to <Button>, so the rendered element carries BOTH components' scope ids, and Button's own unlayered `.btn { display: inline-flex }` has exactly the same specificity as Nav's `.ca-nav-cta { display: none }`. Equal specificity means source order decides, and Button's rule came later in the bundle. THE HIDE SILENTLY DID NOTHING while the sibling change in the same block - un-hiding the search trigger - worked perfectly, so the edit looked correct and half of it was inert. COST: .ca-nav-cta kept its 152px, .ca-nav-actions stayed 327px wide, and the hamburger was pushed to x=555 inside a 390px viewport. The gradient audit measured 555 against 390 on five routes; the shared-blocks gate independently failed the build with "the page scrolls 191px horizontally" on both product pages. FIXED by anchoring both selectors to .ca-nav-actions, which makes them descendant selectors and beats Button's single class outright. !important would also have worked and would have hidden the reason; the anchor is also the honest expression of the rule, since these two are hidden because of WHERE they sit at mobile, not because of anything about the buttons.

issues.title: The /pricing atmosphere amplified the font-swap shift and failed CLS; the field now runs at 768 and above only
issues.note: CAUGHT BY check-cwv ON THE VERY BUILD THAT ADDED IT, 2026-08-05. Giving /pricing the standard section atmosphere took it from CLS 0.1022 to 0.1528 at 390 and failed the 0.1 threshold, with the gate naming the element: b.sv-amb-b, shifting +64px and +20px. THE FIELD IS NOT BUGGY, AND THAT IS THE POINT. The orbs are absolutely positioned with PERCENTAGE offsets against their section, so when the webfont swap re-wraps the text and the section grows, they move with it, and a 520x440 orb moving 64px carries a large impact fraction. A-96 had already attributed one hundred per cent of this site CLS to the font swap. The atmosphere did not create the shift, it MULTIPLIED it. WHY THE FIX IS A BREAKPOINT RATHER THAN A RAISED CEILING. The gate offers both routes in as many words: fix the shift, or record an exception with a ceiling and a reason. Raising the ceiling would have turned the number green without making the page better, on the one route already sitting closest to the threshold. So the cost and the benefit were compared instead. At 390 the orbs are 560px and 520px wide with a 150px blur on a 350px content box, so they are mostly off-screen, heavily blurred, and masked to transparent at the edges. The visible difference is a few units of blue in the corners. Paying 0.05 of CLS for that is a bad trade. THE OWNER OBSERVATION IT ANSWERS IS UNAFFECTED. The complaint was that /pricing was the one page carrying no atmosphere at all, which was a desktop observation, and desktop keeps the field. NOTE FOR ANY FUTURE AMBIENT WORK: a decorative layer positioned in percentages against a container whose height is not stable will always convert somebody else CLS into its own, and the amount scales with the size of the decoration.

issues.title: Board ids are now allocated from a monotonic counter, not from max+1
issues.note: IMPLEMENTS THE FIX A-122 PROPOSED. status/add-issue.js is now the one way to add an item, and it allocates from a nextId counter held in the file rather than by reading the current maximum and adding one. That method was a read-modify-write with no lock: two readers see 108 and both write 109, which is exactly what happened on 2026-08-05 when two terminals allocated A-109 and A-110 to different issues minutes apart. The counter only ever goes up, so an id is never reused even after a deletion. It also validates sev against P1/P2/P3 and status against the board's OWN legend keys, read from the file rather than restated, so the validator cannot drift from the legend it enforces. WHAT IT DOES NOT FIX, stated in the script header so nobody assumes more than it gives: the board is still a whole-file rewrite, so two processes writing at the same instant can still lose one another's entries. Closing that means one file per issue under status/issues/, which is a bigger change than the collision warranted. The standing rule therefore survives: re-read the board immediately before writing and diff the ids you expected against the ids present. There is also a guard that STOPS rather than overwrites if the counter and the file ever disagree, because a silent overwrite on this file is the failure mode with the worst properties - the loser's entries vanish and the item count still looks plausible.

issues.title: Jakarta Fallback re-derived: three of five shipped inputs described no font in this repo
issues.note: CONTROL PASSED FIRST, which is the only reason these numbers moved. The shipped values document their own working in Assets/css/fonts-selfhosted.css and it reproduces to the last digit, so this pass does not disagree with whoever produced them about the arithmetic. It disagrees about THE INPUTS, and each is checkable two independent ways against the binaries in Assets/fonts/. Arial x-height 1062/2048 CORRECT, confirmed by OS/2 sxHeight and by the x outline. Jakarta unitsPerEm 1000 CORRECT. Jakarta x-height 514 WRONG, measured 541/544/546 at 600/700/800 - and 514 is 541 with two digits transposed. Jakarta ascent 964 WRONG, measured 1038 in hhea AND OS/2 sTypo. Jakarta descent 266 WRONG, measured 222 in both. AND THE FORMULA ANSWERED THE WRONG QUESTION: size-adjust was derived as an X-HEIGHT ratio, which keeps the fallback looking the same SIZE, while the stated purpose of the face is that width-dependent layout must not re-wrap, which is an ADVANCE-WIDTH objective. Correcting only the transposition would not have reached it either - a corrected x-height derivation gives 104.91 per cent where width matching needs 108.81. Input errors cost about 5.4pp and the formula choice about 3.9pp, independently. NOW THREE WEIGHT BANDS rather than one number, 107.61 / 108.81 / 109.96 per cent, because the measured spread across the real weight range is 2.35pp and no single value serves all three. Derived twice and the methods had to agree: fontTools summing hmtx over 20,274 characters of the site's REAL heading text, and Chromium laying out the 570 distinct real heading strings, agreeing within 0.13pp at every weight. Verified against the edited file itself: residual under 0.002 per cent on the derivation corpus and under 0.124 per cent on a 1,212-string hold-out never used to derive. The line box is now exactly 1.26000em at every weight, matching the real face, against 1.230em before. line-gap-override: 0 per cent is the ONE shipped value that survives, now verified rather than assumed. A-100 STANDING WARNING RESPECTED AND VINDICATED: xAvgCharWidth was not used, and for the record of how badly it misleads, it claims Inter is 38.27 per cent wider than Arial where real text measures 6.9 per cent.

issues.title: My claim that the weight descriptor blocked the metric re-derivation was FALSE
issues.note: RECORDED AS MY OWN ERROR, 2026-08-05. I held A-100 as blocked on A-131, and told the deriving agent that the ordering was the whole point: that any re-derivation done before the font-weight descriptor was corrected would have measured the browser SYNTHESISED bold rather than the real face. THAT PREMISE IS FALSIFIED, and by measurement rather than argument. Over the same 570 real heading strings, ADVANCE WIDTH IS IDENTICAL AT 400, 600, 700 AND 800, to the last float bit, with and without the weight descriptor present. Synthetic bold in Blink changes PAINT, not ADVANCE. Screenshot ink confirms both halves: without the descriptor, weight 700 paints 39 per cent more ink at the SAME 888px advance, and with it, 700 and 800 are pixel-identical to 400. So the width derivation would have produced the same answer a day earlier, and the item was held for a reason that did not exist. THE WEIGHT FIX WAS STILL A REAL FIX - a synthesised bold is the wrong shape and the browser was making one - it simply was not a precondition for this. WHAT I SHOULD HAVE DONE is what I asked the agent to do and did not do myself: test the premise before acting on it. I reasoned from a plausible mechanism, wrote it into the board and into the agent brief as established fact, and it took an agent measuring it to find out. Left as a CLEARED entry rather than deleted, because the pattern is the point: an ordering constraint asserted from a mechanism nobody measured is exactly the class of stale claim this session has spent the night correcting in other people's comments.

issues.title: Inter had no metric fallback at all, and the re-derivation reproduced the recorded numbers to a quarter of a point
issues.note: Inter is 93.4 PER CENT OF ALL SITE TEXT, 63,889 characters at weight 400, and has NO metric-matched fallback at all. Its real swap partner here is Segoe UI, not Arial: system-ui resolves to Segoe UI on this machine, measured, so any derivation against Arial describes the wrong comparison. A-96 PARTLY REPRODUCES AND PARTLY DOES NOT, and the part that does not is instructive. Its 3.7 per cent at weight 700 is CONFIRMED, measured 3.54 to 3.91 per cent against Segoe UI. Its 10.4 per cent on the /terms list is NOT reproduced: over the actual 97 list-item strings on /terms and /security, all Inter 400, the measured gap is 7.55 per cent. A-96 appears to have measured ONE shrink-wrapped li box going 252.95 to 279.17, and a wrapped box width is set by where the line break happens to fall, which scales the underlying difference arbitrarily. That is the same class of error as the 9.61 per cent figure that came from a single string. The gap also runs OPPOSITE to the obvious reading: it SHRINKS with weight, 7.55 per cent at 400 down to 3.5 per cent at 700, because Segoe UI Bold widens more than Inter does. Segoe UI line box is 1.33em against Inter 1.21em, a 9.9 per cent mismatch. NUMBERS DERIVED AND READY, single value optimised for weight 400 which is 93.4 per cent of the text: size-adjust 106.93 per cent, ascent-override 90.60, descent-override 22.56, line-gap-override 0. Banded values for 400/500/600/700 are also derived. NOT SHIPPED because it needs --font-body in tokens.css to name the new face, which is a wider blast radius than this board item authorised. Browser-validated for the single-value variant; the banded rows are arithmetic and not separately measured. || SHIPPED 2026-08-05. Inter is 93.4 PER CENT OF ALL TEXT on this site and had NO metric-matched fallback, where the display face has had three derived bands since this morning. Every character of body copy re-laid out on swap. THE CONTROL RAN FIRST AND IT PASSED, which is the only reason these numbers are trusted rather than merely plausible. This item already carried proposed values from an earlier pass - size-adjust 106.93, ascent 90.60, descent 22.56 - and the reason for re-deriving rather than shipping them was internal: the note's own headline measurement was 7.55 per cent while its size-adjust said 6.93, and those cannot both describe one measurement. Re-derived by a different route in scripts/derive-inter-fallback.mjs, Chromium over 529 real body strings taken from the built output and laid out at 400px: Segoe UI 106.66 against 106.93, ascent 90.83 against 90.60, descent 22.61 against 22.56. TWO INDEPENDENT DERIVATIONS A QUARTER OF A POINT APART. The measured values ship because they are the ones validated end to end. VALIDATED, NOT MERELY CALCULATED: with the descriptors applied the same 529 strings measure at residual 1.00000 against real Inter, and the line box lands on 1.2100em, Inter's own 1984/2048 ascent plus 494/2048 descent. Both halves measured in the browser. TWO FACES BECAUSE ONE local() CANNOT COVER TWO PLATFORMS: system-ui resolves to Segoe UI on Windows and SF Pro on macOS, 3.1pp apart in width, so one set of overrides is wrong for one of them. Inter Fallback pins Segoe at 106.66 and Inter Fallback Arial pins Arial at 103.50, listed in that order in --font-body. SF Pro is deliberately absent for the same reason Arial Bold is absent from the Jakarta chain - it could not be measured from this machine and a band that silently caught an underived face would carry an unknown error. AND MY OWN HARNESS WAS WRONG TWICE BEFORE IT WAS RIGHT, both caught by the numbers being absurd rather than by reading the code: the first run reported Inter jumping 18.7 per cent in advance width between weight 400 and 500, which no weight axis does, because document.fonts.ready resolves when PENDING loads settle and a face nothing has laid out yet is not pending - so the first measurement of every run silently returned the default serif. It needs an explicit fonts.load() for the exact size-and-weight string. The corpus was also splitting on a stray control byte instead of the newline, so each FILE arrived as one string; caught because the reported string count and character count could not both be true of the same array.

issues.title: Independent verification refuted one claim and found four defects, including a WCAG 2.2.2 Level A failure
issues.note: AN AGENT THAT MADE NONE OF THE CHANGES VERIFIED fb1977e8 ADVERSARIALLY, 2026-08-05. FOUR OF FIVE CLAIMS CONFIRMED with numbers: hover, 428 elements hovered across 7 routes at 1440 and 205 tapped at 390, zero layout changes, zero new hues, zero touch latches; overflow, 43 routes by 6 widths, 258 measurements, zero overflow; headings and alt, all 43 routes have exactly one h1, zero heading skips, 49 images all with alt, plus zero duplicate ids and zero unlabelled controls; and reduced motion, zero long or infinite animations on any route. THE CONTRAST CLAIM WAS REFUTED and the failure is the kind computed styles cannot see: the Ctrl K hint in the header measures 3.70 to 3.94:1 against the 4.5:1 that 11px text needs, on 12 to 17 routes, because the header is a translucent color-mix over a backdrop-filter so its true backdrop is whatever the page is behind it - 9.1:1 over a dark body, failing over a light one. FOUR NEW DEFECTS, ALL NOW FIXED. HIGH, and a WCAG 2.2.2 Level A conformance failure: the product-page carousel pause never worked, measured by holding hover for 11 seconds and watching the index go 4 to 6, and holding keyboard focus and watching it go 0 to 2. The animation SHORTHAND resets animation-play-state to running and sat at higher specificity than the paused longhand, and since the advance is driven by animationend nothing ever paused - while the component comment asserted the mechanism worked, the third lying comment found tonight. Fixed by driving play-state from an inherited variable in the SAME rule as the shorthand, so specificity cannot re-enter, rather than by out-specifying it and leaving the trap armed. A real pause BUTTON was added too, because hover is unavailable on touch and focus-within resumes the moment a reader tabs away, so neither is a mechanism in the sense the criterion means. MEDIUM: six dead in-page anchors on /terms, the only route of 43 with any, because the cards link to unprefixed slugs while the numbered headings emit number-prefixed ids - silent by nature, since a dead fragment throws nothing and leaves the reader where they were. MEDIUM: the Ctrl K contrast above, now --c-text-sub at 5.75:1 on the same measured backdrop. LOW: the carousel tablist had no roving tabindex, so eight tabs meant eight tab stops; the arrow keys were already implemented, so the ARIA pattern was half-built and the missing half was the one a reader feels. WHAT MAKES THE REPORT TRUSTWORTHY IS WHAT IT THREW AWAY: its own bulk sweep raised 120 contrast failures and it disproved all of them before reporting - 30 an anti-aliasing bias in its median statistic, 5 layout-shift artefacts it re-measured individually, and one scare traced to its own kill-stylesheet leaking. It also flagged that another process was editing the tree mid-run, so its findings hold for dist at fb1977e8 and the source has since diverged.

issues.title: Two 2.8MB scratch build directories were untracked and unignored, and were being type-checked
issues.note: FOUND 2026-08-05 by noticing astro check hints jump from 13 to 31 and asking why rather than dismissing them as noise. astro/dist-before and astro/dist-after, 2.8MB each, left by an agent doing a before-and-after comparison. BUILDING TO A SCRATCH outDir IS THE RIGHT INSTINCT and should not be discouraged: astro/dist is read by the gates and by the review server on :8095, so an agent that rebuilt it to measure its own change would corrupt everyone else readings. The defect is only that nothing ignored the result. TWO CONSEQUENCES: .gitignore covered dist/ but not dist-before/ or dist-after/, so both were untracked-but-not-ignored and would have entered the next commit; and astro check was walking their emitted .mjs and reporting ts(6133) warnings from GENERATED code as though they were source, which is where 23 of the 31 hints came from. Removed, and .gitignore now matches dist-*/ by suffix rather than the two exact names, because the next agent will choose a different one. ALSO CLEANED, and it is real dead code rather than noise: five gate scripts - check-breadcrumbs, check-glossary-filter, check-heading-ink, check-sheen and check-timeline - still imported node:fs after the A-99 extraction moved their file reading into the shared dist-server helper. Each was verified genuinely unused before removal and all five still parse. Hints are now 8, down from 31. NONE OF THIS WOULD HAVE BROKEN ANYTHING, and that is the argument for doing it: 23 spurious hints are exactly how a real one gets missed.

issues.title: A-103, A-111 and A-113 cut as one job: the animation ratchet is flat and teal is off every ambient field
issues.note: MEASURED ON THE BUILT PAGE AT 1440. Radial-gradient painters on the homepage 22 to 15, and 16 with ink to 9. Perpetual animations at arrival 20 to 11. AFTER A FULL READ 33 to 11, and back at the top 33 to 11 - THE RATCHET IS FLAT, which was the single most valuable fix and is worth more than deleting any individual orb. Drifting orbs 15 to 6. Reduced motion still returns literally zero at both viewports at three scroll positions. THE RATCHET COST NO OBSERVER. Its measured cause was 13 reveal-started infinite loops, twelve in-spec on the Integrations chips and one fc-spec on the closing card; both are now one-shots with the keyframe percentages rescaled so every fade lands at the same millisecond. That is exactly what BothSides, MarketShape and ReasoningTrace already did under A-104, which is why those three measured clean. Toggling data-lit off on exit was considered and rejected: motion.ts argues that unobserve is what makes once true, and un-setting it would restage every one-shot beat each time a reader scrolled past a section twice. check-motion observer allow-list stays at four. TEAL IS NOW ABSENT FROM EVERY AMBIENT FIELD ON THE HOMEPAGE and each section carries one hue-bearing light, which is A-113 in one sentence: teal means verified and orchid means refused, and both were being spent as haze across five sections at once. Mean hero-band chroma over 20 fixed points 23.3 to 15.5; the hero right pole from chroma 52 to 5; whole-page pixels at chroma 12 or above 43.2 per cent to 39.6 per cent. CONTRAST HELD: 48 text nodes across the six touched sections, judged against the brightest pixel of the painted ground inside each node own box, zero fell by more than 0.05 and two rose. TWO PIECES OF DISCIPLINE WORTH KEEPING. A first attempt matched the cyan field LUMINANCE, which was arithmetically right and produced grey fog, because a neutral lift over near-black has no hue to be attributed to and reads as dirt; five candidate fills were rendered before one shipped. And the before-and-after pixel comparison across two builds was DISCARDED as untrustworthy because another agent rewrote fonts.css and tokens.css between them, so every colour claim above is an A/B inside a single build with the old rig reconstructed in the live document and then removed. FOLLOW-ON, THE BIGGEST PIECE: .sv-amb in styles/surfaces.css is the SHARED section rig and still runs teal plus violet. It does not appear on the homepage, so this cut did not reach it, and certifying the 43 routes it does reach was out of scope.

issues.title: --grad-beam painted teal on 13 elements while two call sites asked for something else
issues.note: A CONSEQUENCE OF MY OWN FIX THAT I DID NOT ENUMERATE. When A-130 inlined the dead knobs in --grad-beam and --grad-fade, I recorded that the affected renders were left deliberately unfixed and made explicable rather than corrected. I listed three. There was a fourth class I missed, found by the ambient cut measuring the built page: THREE CALL SITES SET --beam-hue BELIEVING IT WORKS, and all three painted teal. FinalCta.astro:444 asked for WHITE, and its own comment claimed a white bloom rather than a hue while the closing card swept teal. MarketShape.astro:713 asked for the stop accent via currentColor. Integrations.astro:1307 set nothing and took the default across twelve connector chips. So thirteen elements were painting the VERIFIED pigment as pure decoration. THE FIX IS NOT TO MAKE THE KNOB WORK. A travelling light sweeping a panel edge is not the element a section is about, so under the gradient rule the owner approved on 2026-08-05 it may carry no hue at all: hue is permitted once per section, on the element the section is about, and never on a control or under text. --grad-beam is now achromatic, a white core with a white bloom at 45 per cent, which is a luminance ramp and permitted anywhere. The two dead --beam-hue declarations are deleted rather than left to mislead, each with a note saying why. BothSides had already worked this out independently and written its beam literally at its point of use with the trap documented, so the codebase contained both the defect and its own diagnosis, in two files, for some time.

issues.title: check-render marks an allow-list entry STALE on a race, and I deleted a live exception on one report
issues.note: A ROUND TRIP THAT COST TWO BUILDS, 2026-08-05, and the gate defect is the durable half. check-render annotates any ALLOW_BESPOKE entry that matched nothing in a run as [STALE - matches nothing], and the file convention is that the list may only shrink, so a STALE entry reads as an instruction to delete. I deleted .tabsw__tab on one such report. THE VERY NEXT BUILD FAILED on .tabsw__tab For suppliers, with nothing about the page changed between the two runs. THE MARKER IS UNRELIABLE FOR ANY TIMING-DEPENDENT CONTROL. The bespoke-button rule fires on a control that has padding AND a painted background or border, and on this switcher ONLY THE SELECTED TAB HAS A FILL - unselected ones are transparent until chosen. So whether the entry matches anything depends on whether the tablist had been upgraded by its script and painted at the instant the measurement was taken. That is a race, not a fact about the code, and a gate that reports a race as a durable state will keep inviting this deletion. WHAT I GOT WRONG IS SUBTLER THAN THE DELETION and is the same error I recorded against myself in A-151 two hours earlier: I checked that the element still existed, saw that it did, and then INFERRED the mechanism - the rule no longer reaches it because unselected tabs are transparent. That inference was plausible, internally consistent, and wrong, and I acted on it without measuring. Entry restored with the round trip written into its own reason so the next reader does not repeat it. THE GATE FIX, not done here: either re-check a candidate STALE entry against every state the control can be in, or drop the marker to advisory wording that does not read as an instruction. Deleting a live exception silently re-arms whatever it was suppressing. || GATE FIXED 2026-08-05, both halves. check-render now asks a SECOND question that the old marker never asked: is anything in the DOM carrying this selector at all, independently of whether the rule fired on it? The four used* sets only ever recorded that a rule FIRED and an allow-list entry caught it, so a live entry on a state-dependent control registered as nothing and got annotated STALE - matches nothing, which under this file's may-only-shrink convention reads as an instruction to delete. That is what cost two builds. A per-route querySelector census now splits one misleading marker into two honest ones: DORMANT - in the DOM, rule did not fire this run; do NOT delete, against STALE - no element carries it on any route; safe to remove. The wording is deliberate in both directions - DORMANT names the consequence because nothing in the old text told a reader to stop, and STALE now states the evidence it actually rests on rather than the much stronger thing the old phrasing implied. The census cannot fail a build: an unparseable selector is skipped, because a diagnostic that can break the gate it annotates is worse than the marker it replaces.

issues.title: The 834 two-card stacking survived its own fix because the element carries both card-row classes
issues.note: THE 2026-08-05 AUDIT CALLED THIS THE SINGLE WORST FIDELITY DEFECT, and it was fixed twice. At 834 the concept keeps the two ProofGate cards side by side at 383px each and the build stacked them full width. THE FIRST FIX LOOKED CORRECT AND DID NOTHING. It removed .card-row--eight-four from the shared 56rem collapse list and gave the modifier its own collapse at the concept 768, which is the right shape. Re-measuring after it: the cards were STILL 786px at 834, unchanged. THE REASON IS ONE THE SELECTOR LIST HIDES. The element is class=card-row card-row--eight-four, so it carries BOTH names, and the bare .card-row selector was still in that same collapse list. Removing the modifier from a list does not exempt an element whose BASE class is also in it - the base rule matched, collapsed the grid to one track at 896, and the 6/6 step declared at 1024 had no multi-track template left to sit in. The exemption has to be stated on the base selector, .card-row:not(.card-row--eight-four), which is what now ships. THIS IS THE THIRD TIME TONIGHT A FIX LOOKED RIGHT AND DID NOTHING, and all three were only visible by measuring the rendered result rather than reading the change: the nav CTA hide that lost a specificity tie to Button.astro and gave every route horizontal scroll; the carousel pause defeated by the animation shorthand resetting play-state; and this. In each case the diff was persuasive and the page disagreed.

issues.title: The reported WebKit carousel-image defect does not reproduce, and the fix proposed for it would have been a regression
issues.note: DID NOT REPRODUCE, measured across three engines 2026-08-05. The Playwright pass reported that the FIRST carousel slide on /crowmark/ and /crowmark-buyers/ is loading=lazy and never completes in WebKit even after 20 seconds of polling, and recommended loading=eager with fetchpriority=high on the first slide of every carousel. Probed directly in chromium, webkit AND firefox against the built output: in all three, after the carousel is scrolled into view, slide 1 reports complete=true with naturalWidth 2880, and there are ZERO non-2xx image responses on either route. The symptom is possibility two of three - the test polled .complete without ever scrolling the element into view, and a lazy image 4,769px down is behaving exactly as specified by not loading. THE PROPOSED FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN A REAL REGRESSION, and this is why an agent recommendation is not acted on before the mechanism is checked. A-93 measured these offsets deliberately: the first slide sits 5,905px down at 1440 and 8,596px at 390 on /crowmark, six to ten screens below the fold, and it is the LARGEST single asset on the route. Eager-loading it puts the site's biggest image at the loader's highest priority in competition with the LCP element of a page the reader has not begun to scroll - which is the precise defect A-93 was raised to fix, and the default was set to false on purpose. WHAT THE PROBE DID FIND, and it is also not a defect: the AVIF source carries a five-rung ladder plus sizes while the WebP source carries a single 2880px master, so a WebKit without AVIF fetches 196,112 B to paint 1065 CSS px where AVIF serves 40,405 B, 4.9 times the bytes. That asymmetry is DELIBERATE and measured, recorded against the LADDER constant in Carousel.astro and beside the wholeBuild budget: a WebP ladder took the build from 12,541 KB to 17,831 KB against a 14,336 KB budget, with 55 per cent of the growth being WebP nobody would fetch, and the WebP tier is already larger than the PNG tier on all 16 of 16 files. The affected population is Safari below 16.4 only, on an image six screens down. Left as it stands.

issues.title: The two autoplaying components now have a behavioural gate, and writing it caught the gate itself reading a record instead of the thing
issues.note: ADDED scripts/check-autoplay.mjs 2026-08-05, wired as the 33rd link of the build chain. WHY A GATE AND NOT A CHECK: the carousel on this site once carried a comment stating its pause worked while hovering it for 11 seconds advanced it from slide 4 to slide 6 - a WCAG 2.2.2 Level A failure that every reader of the source was told was handled. A-104 then added TWO more autoplaying components with three NON-OPTIONAL constraints, and nothing measured any of them. The gate reads no source at all: it starts the real page, waits real time and reads the resulting state. 14 behavioural checks over both components. VERIFIED PASSING: neither moves under prefers-reduced-motion; neither reveals a pause control while no timer runs, so there is never a control that cannot do anything; both offer a visible pause at 91x44 and 115x44, comfortably over the 24px floor; PRESSING each one actually stops the thing, checked by driving it rather than by finding it in the DOM; and the tab switcher stops permanently once a reader picks a tab, still on the chosen tab 16 seconds later. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL, three separate injections into dist producing five distinct failing assertions: hiding both pause controls fails the WCAG check and the target-size check on both components; revealing a pause control under reduced motion fails the dead-control check on both; and a third injection failed too. AND THE GATE MADE THE EXACT MISTAKE IT EXISTS TO CATCH, which is the part worth keeping. Its first version asserted that data-band flips to off when a reader pauses the trust band. It failed. The defect was the ASSERTION, not the site: data-band records whether the band is ALLOWED to move at all, which is the reduced-motion gate, and it correctly stays on when a reader pauses. Measured properly the track holds position across 600ms and 2.6s while the button relabels to Resume scrolling, so the pause always worked and the gate was reading a record of the thing rather than the thing. Rewritten to measure TRAVEL: sampled at 500ms intervals the band moves about 119px in three seconds, so roughly 40px/s, giving ~47px of travel in the 1200ms window against 0 when paused. ONE FURTHER CORRECTION, established by falsification rather than by reading the stylesheet: injecting transform:none onto .in__track did NOT stop the band, which is only explicable if something above it carries the transform. The in-band keyframe runs on .in__rail, the PARENT of TWO .in__track elements, because the marquee duplicates the row to loop seamlessly. So .in__track reads animationName none while plainly moving. The gate reads a rect precisely because getBoundingClientRect composes ancestor transforms and therefore does not care where in the subtree the movement is produced.

issues.title: Homepage accessibility and reflow re-verified after the night's changes, clean at four viewports
issues.note: MEASURED 2026-08-05 against dist at commit 67012219, after a night that changed the homepage substantially - autoplay on the product tabs, the trust band, the ProofGate copy, a new section order and a new body font stack. axe-core run over wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and wcag22aa at 1440x900, 834x1112, 390x844 and 320x568, under reduced motion with every animation drained first so nothing was read mid-arrival. ZERO violations at all four. Also zero horizontal scroll at all four: scrollWidth equals innerWidth exactly at 1440, 834, 390 and 320, which matters because A-81 previously found three routes scrolling at 320 and 320 is the narrowest viewport WCAG 1.4.10 Reflow contemplates. PROVEN ABLE TO FAIL rather than assumed, because a scan reporting nothing is indistinguishable from a scan that is not running: injecting an image with no alt, a button with no accessible name and a 1.3:1 paragraph into dist produced exactly those three violations, image-alt and button-name as critical and color-contrast as serious, at every viewport; restoring the file returned it to zero. The scan is genuinely reaching the page.

directives.text: Enforce centrally and automatically. Never manual patching.
directives.note: The one I have broken most.

directives.text: 'Adopt similar' means STYLE AND DESIGN ONLY; everything else stays as the current build.
Keep the terminal clean; use background agents and parallel execution.
'As per architecture and design' means genuine BEST PRACTICE, not whatever we previously recorded as agreed. A prior decision is evidence, not authority.
One semantic per hue, and violet is spoken for: violet means the engine REFUSED something. No other role may enter that hue family.
No justification-by-assertion in code comments or data files. A file may not state a reason that is not true of the tree.
No conceded field returns without Aparajita signing it off in writing.
Centre up to 3 lines; left-align beyond. A line count is a rendered fact, so the gate for it must measure the painted page.
